title: Likes and interests: szeret and érdekel

sections.title: Three ways to say it
sections.content: To say you like a particular thing, use *szeret* with the object. You know the thing, so the verb takes its definite ending, as *kérem* does, and the thing takes *-t*: *Szeretem a zenét.* To say you like doing something, use the indefinite ending and an infinitive, the *-ni* form you know from *szoktam olvasni*: *Szeretek olvasni.* The third way has no *szeret*: *A sport érdekel.* (Sport interests me.) Here the thing is the subject, so it has no *-t*.

sections.title: Three patterns
rows: I like music. (a thing: definite ending and -t)
Sport interests me. (the thing is the subject)

sections.title: Who is interested?
sections.content: With *érdekel* the person is left out unless you want to stress it. To say "you" or "me" use *téged* and *engem*: *Téged érdekel a sport?* (Does sport interest you?) *Engem érdekel a zene.* (Music interests me.) The verb stays *érdekel*.
Do not add *-t* after *érdekel*: *A sport érdekel*, not *A sportot érdekel*. The thing that interests you is the subject of the sentence, not the object.
